GWAS Summary Statistics Subset

Source: R/data.R
gwas_subset.Rd

A curated subset of GWAS Catalog summary statistics prepared for pleiotropy analysis.

Usage

gwas_subset

Format

A data.table with 2498 rows and 5 columns:

SNPS

Character. SNP identifiers (rs numbers)

MAPPED_TRAIT

Character. Standardized trait or phenotype name

PVALUE_MLOG

Numeric. -log10 transformed p-values for significance

CHR_ID

Character. Chromosome identifier (1-22, X, Y)

CHR_POS

Numeric. Chromosomal position in base pairs

Source

GWAS Catalog associations file (2024 release), downloaded from: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/api/search/downloads/alternative

The subset was created by data-raw/create_gwas_subset.R: 1. Loading the complete GWAS Catalog associations file 2. Selecting 15 traits relevant to complex disease and metabolism 3. Collapsing duplicate study entries to one row per SNP-trait pair (keeping the most significant association) 4. Retaining all associations of the strongest pleiotropic SNPs, then filling with a trait-balanced random sample to reach ~2500 rows 5. Ensuring representation across multiple chromosomes

Details

This dataset contains genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the GWAS Catalog (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/), reduced to a small, reproducible set that demonstrates pleiotropy detection and visualization. It is the example dataset shipped with `pleior`.

The dataset contains 2498 associations covering 1835 distinct SNPs across 15 traits. Of these SNPs, 128 are pleiotropic (associated with two or more of the 15 traits); the strongest, rs429358 (in the APOE region), maps to 12 traits. rs814573, used as a running example in the README, is associated with myocardial infarction and C-reactive protein measurement in this subset.

The 15 traits are:

  • body mass index

  • body height

  • Alzheimer disease

  • myocardial infarction

  • coronary artery disease

  • type 2 diabetes mellitus

  • systolic blood pressure

  • diastolic blood pressure

  • low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement

  • high density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement

  • triglyceride measurement

  • total cholesterol measurement

  • C-reactive protein measurement

  • asthma

  • schizophrenia

The data is suitable for:

  • Demonstrating pleiotropy detection (SNPs associated with multiple traits)

  • Testing visualization functions

  • Teaching GWAS analysis workflows

  • Benchmarking analysis methods

References

GWAS Catalog Team. (2024). GWAS Catalog: a knowledgebase for genome-wide association studies. *Nucleic Acids Research*, 51(D1), D944-D949. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkab1009

Examples

# Load the data
data(gwas_subset)
head(gwas_subset)
#>           SNPS                                    MAPPED_TRAIT PVALUE_MLOG
#>         <char>                                          <char>       <num>
#> 1: rs115866895                                     body height   13.698970
#> 2: rs560221037 low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement   11.221849
#> 3:  rs12081179                         systolic blood pressure    7.522879
#> 4:   rs4908677                                     body height    7.522879
#> 5:   rs6682378                                 body mass index    9.698970
#> 6:   rs1381928                                          asthma    8.397940
#>    CHR_ID CHR_POS
#>    <char>   <num>
#> 1:      1 1661177
#> 2:      1 2235046
#> 3:      1 2319680
#> 4:      1 7678120
#> 5:      1 8071697
#> 6:      1 8630874

# Basic statistics
n_unique_snps <- length(unique(gwas_subset$SNPS))
n_unique_traits <- length(unique(gwas_subset$MAPPED_TRAIT))
cat("Unique SNPs:", n_unique_snps, "\n")
#> Unique SNPs: 1835 
cat("Unique traits:", n_unique_traits, "\n")
#> Unique traits: 15 

# Preprocess and detect pleiotropy
gwas_clean <- preprocess_gwas(gwas_subset, pvalue_threshold = 1e-5)
pleio_results <- detect_pleiotropy(gwas_clean)
head(pleio_results)
